data.narrative:
RoboTwin is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Megi Mejdrechová, Ladislav Dvořák, and David Polák. The company has raised €2.3M in EIC funding. The broader robotics and manufacturing sector includes one public comparable (ticker 277810.KQ) and eight private peers, including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI.

The valuation analysis employs stage-progression methodology as the primary triangulation approach. Given the limited peer dataset at seed stage, traditional peer-median comparables are not applicable—the sector contains ten robotics companies overall, but insufficient overlap in stage, adjacency, or valuation tier to support a robust median multiple. The stage-progression method applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier to the €2.3M capital raised proxy, yielding an implied valuation of approximately $6M.

This analysis supports a valuation range of $5M to $7M, with $6M as the median point. The range reflects a ±15% bandwidth around the stage-progression output. Key uncertainties include the absence of narrowly comparable seed-stage robotics peers, limiting confidence in stage-specific multiple validation, and reliance on total raised as a valuation proxy rather than observable market transactions. The single-method approach necessitates caution; validation through additional financing data or sector-specific benchmarks would strengthen conviction.
